title: Contacts as Avro
prompt: The event platform takes contacts as Avro files. Write `save(contacts, path)` so it saves the contacts at `path` as Avro. `solve` is written for you: it saves them and reads the folder back as Avro.
rules: Save every contact with every column, as Avro, at `path`.
The folder may already hold an earlier export: replace it, don't add to it.
`solve` returns what reading the folder gives: the columns of `contacts`, in the same order, with the same types.
Keep repeated rows. An empty table gives an empty export.
hints: Avro is written through the general writer: `format(...)`, then `save(path)`.
Writing to a folder that already exists fails unless you choose a mode.
`.mode("overwrite")` replaces the folder; `append` would leave the old rows next to the new ones.
explanation: One line does it: `contacts.write.mode("overwrite").format("avro").save(path)`. Avro keeps the schema inside the file, so `is_primary` comes back as a boolean and the columns keep their order without any read options. `overwrite` matters because the folder is there from the run before; the default mode raises an error and `append` doubles the rows. Writing Parquet or JSON instead fails here, because the folder is read as Avro.
